title: Venezuelan Lentil Dumplings
description: Fresh and juicy dumplings filled with a mix of brown lentils, onions, garlic, and spices, perfect for a date night in. Inspired by the flavors of Venezuela, these dumplings are diabetic-friendly and easy to make.
instructions: In a large pan, heat the olive oil over medium heat.
Add the chopped onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute, stirring constantly.
In a separate bowl, mix together the cooked lentils, chopped cilantro, salt, and black pepper.
Using a pastry blender or your fingers, work the lentil mixture into the whole wheat flour until just combined.
Gradually add the egg replacer or beaten egg and mix until the dough comes together.
Knead the dough for about 10 minutes until it becomes smooth and elastic.
Divide the dough into 8 equal pieces and roll each piece into a ball.
Use a rolling pin to flatten each ball into a disk shape.
Place a tablespoon of the lentil mixture in the center of each disk and fold the dough over to form a half-moon shape.
Seal the edges by pressing them with a fork.
In a large pot of boiling, salted water, cook the dumplings for 10-12 minutes, or until they float to the surface.
Remove the dumplings from the water with a slotted spoon and serve hot, topped with vegan mozzarella cheese if desired.
To make the tomato sauce, heat the olive oil in a separate pan over medium heat.
Add the tomato paste and cook, stirring constantly, for about 2 minutes.
Add the water and stir to combine.
Bring the sauce to a simmer and cook for about 5 minutes, or until thickened.
Serve the dumplings with the tomato sauce spooned over the top.
